subject: Dedicated capacity — sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — sizing follow-up

Hi Olivia / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the Acme team. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Summary of what we heard:
- Use case: real-time customer support assistant + post-chat summarization for chat history indexing.
- Current RPS baseline: ~5 TPS today, wanting to scale to steady-state 20–30 TPS during daytime retail hours with spikes to ~60 TPS for promotions.
- Desired latency: 200–400ms p95 for responses.
- Typical prompt size / token mix: prompt ~400–800 tokens, average response ~250–500 tokens (avg total ~1.2k tokens/request).
- Security: VPC private deployment preferred, but open to Dedicated (reserved GPU fleet) if VPC is a blocker for timeline.

Questions / ask for you: can you confirm peak sustained TPS target (steady-state vs burst), and whether any batch/async workflows can tolerate higher latency? Also pls share the token mix for the dashboarding/test set if available.

Planned next steps from Redwood:
- Rafa / infra to propose GPU options (H100 vs A100) and a recommended dedicated pool configuration based on your TPS + token mix.
- We'll produce a sizing proposal and cost estimate (PDF + sizing sheet).
- If Dedicated looks good we can scope a 30–60 day delivery from PO to production (private VPC will add ~2–3 weeks).

Attaching: redwood-sizing-sheet.xlsx (blank template) — please populate the sample traffic rows if you have them.

If that looks right I'll loop Rafael with a formal proposal.

Thanks,
Marissa
Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. Confirming numbers from our side:

- Steady-state target: 25 TPS (daytime traffic).
- Burst target: up to 75 TPS for short promotional bursts (2–10 minutes).
- Concurrency: we expect ~40 concurrent open chats during peak (but we can provision for 100 concurrent sessions to be safe).
- Token mix: average request seen in our sample traces is ~1.1k tokens (prompt + response). We attached a small export of 1,000 sample requests in the sizing sheet.
- Latency: 300ms p95 desired, but up to 600ms acceptable on rare bursts.
- Preferred GPU: we're open, but procurement prefers cost-efficient options. If H100 provides materially better latency/cost, we'd consider it.
- Security: we require VPC networking and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Procurement contact: Tom Barnes (cc) — he'll handle PO and contract.

Let us know recommended configuration and rough monthly cost estimate. Looking forward to the proposal.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Product Integrations | Acme Retail
olivia.chen@acmeretail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — sizing follow-up (Acme)

Rafa / Aditya — forwarding Olivia's confirmation + sample traffic. Key constraints: steady 25 TPS, bursts to 75 TPS, ~1.1k avg tokens, target 300ms p95, VPC required.

Preliminary recommendation (quick gut):
- Fleet: Dedicated capacity with burstable nodes + VPC networking.
- GPU profile: 4x H100 (80GB) for steady-state, with ability to add 2 additional nodes for bursts (autoscale policy). H100 gives headroom for low-latency p95 at this token mix. If cost is a hard constraint, a 6x A100 (80GB) config can be considered — slightly higher latency but lower unit cost in some regions.
- Concurrency / threads: configure target concurrency per device so we can sustain 25 TPS @ ~1.1k tokens with batching window ~20ms. Expected concurrency per H100: ~20–30 concurrent token-streaming requests depending on model.
- Model: recommend a quantized Llama-variant or a TSM-optimized model; will run benchmarks in-house against their sample to pick lowest cost config that meets 300ms p95.
- Caching: enable prefix caching for common templates to reduce cost on repeated prompts.

Action items for proposal:
1) Run benchmark against their sample traces (Aditya) — bench both H100 and A100, measuring p95 and cost/1k tokens.
2) Generate PDF proposal with target config, cost, and timeline (Rafael).
3) Prepare SOC2 attestation and VPC onboarding checklist for procurement (Marissa).

If you want I can draft the PO terms and timeline for procurement (Tom).

—Marissa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-30T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RDW Proposal: Dedicated capacity sizing + cost estimate (Acme)

Hi Olivia / Tom — attaching our formal proposal (RDW-scaling-proposal-v2.pdf) and the completed sizing sheet. High level:

- Recommended initial config: 4x H100 (80GB) Dedicated pool, autoscale + 2 burst nodes.
- Estimated steady-state throughput: ~28 TPS at 1.1k token average, expected p95 ~250–320ms depending on model choice.
- Burst capacity: autoscale to 6 nodes for short promotion bursts (up to 75 TPS).
- Monthly estimated cost (incl. reserved capacity discount): $XX,XXX/month (detailed line items in attached PDF).
- Timeline: 2–3 weeks for Dedicated setup and VPC peering; 4–6 weeks for full production rollout including benchmarks and testing.

Attachments: RDW-scaling-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal) — redwood-sizing-sheet.xlsx (completed sample).

Next steps:
1) Procurement to review PO/contract terms (Tom).
2) Once PO signed we schedule a 1-week bench run to finalize model and kernel choices.
3) Kick off VPC peering and security review (SOC2 evidence attached in portal link).

Tom — happy to review the contract and adjust payment terms if needed.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
